lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.32 - A Look and learn

details: Look and learn presents the grammar rules for prepositions of time. It clearly categorises the use of 'at', 'on', and 'in' with specific examples for students to study.
Look for students focusing on the grammar table and correctly identifying which preposition to use with a time, a day, or a month.

“Who wants to go the circus? The circus takes place in a tent, at 7pm each evening in March. If you want to come, I need you to pay attention to the small words I’m using that tell us 'when': at, on, and in.”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.32 - B. Write at, on, or in

details: Write at, on, or in provides controlled practice of the grammar rule. Students read the paragraph and complete the sentences with the correct preposition of time to show their understanding.
Look for the correct use of 'at', 'on', and 'in' in the blanks, showing that students can apply the rules from the grammar table.
“My friend Ella is going to come with us to the circus. She’s written us a letter to introduce herself. Can you read it and write the correct prepositions in the gaps for her?”

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book p.116-118 - A Point and say

details: Point and say prepares students for the story by activating vocabulary. Students look at the pictures, identify characters and objects and predict what might happen at the circus.
Look for students actively pointing to details in the pictures and sharing simple ideas or predictions about the story.

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book p.116-118 - B Listen and read

details: Listen and read develops reading fluency and comprehension. Students follow along with the audio, connecting the written words to the story's events and the spoken narration.
Look for students following the text with their finger, paying attention to the story, and showing understanding of the main events.

lessonPlan.topic: Phonics Book p.116-118 - D Say the story with your friends

details: Say the story with your friends provides fluency practice through retelling. Students work in groups to narrate the story in their own words or act out the dialogue, building speaking confidence.
Look for confident retelling of the main story points, active participation within the group, and clear pronunciation.
